newsitem.title: USA: Union boss - pilots flying after 24-minute stoppage.
newsitem.headline: Union boss - pilots flying after 24-minute stoppage.

text.p: American Airlines pilots are back in the cockpit after a 24-minute stoppage, but may have to suspend flights again if a 60-day cooling-off period does not end in a solution, their union chief said early on Saturday.

"The pilots are doing their jobs, they are back flying their aircraft," Allied Pilots Association President James Sovich told reporters after President Bill Clinton formed an emergency board to stop his pilots' midnight (0500 GMT) strike.

Sovich said of Clinton's intervention, which followed a marathon effort by federal mediators: "I've spent half my life in mediation. This is one more time. If ... what comes out of the presidential emergency board is not acceptable, we will start into another cooling-off period.

"What I passed on to our membership tonight is plan on at least 60 days, reach down into your gut after that because we may have to do this one more time, where we shut down the airline for a second time."
He said his members would have preferred it if Clinton had not intervened, but they respected his action and would comply.
"Those that did get out (of their planes) -- as it turned out, that 24-minute period did capture several of our folks -- if asked to, they'll get out of their airplanes again," he said.
